text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for reaching out, C. I am sorry about your dad. I will contact A and B so all three of you can be heard. To start a shared list of concerns (I call them NCEs), could you tell me what matters most to you? For example, is your concern the size of the discount, how the house is valued, or how the money is split? Also, who is the executor, and does the will say how the house should be divided? Please correct me if I have anything wrong.

My main concern is getting a fair share based on a proper valuation. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount, and I won’t subsidize it. I’m not sure who the executor is or what the will says about the house—we’ll need to check.

Hello A. I am sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three sisters agree on a plan for the house. I understand you and your husband would like to buy it. Could you tell me what matters most to you, what price or discount you have in mind, and why? I am keeping a shared list of everyone's concerns, and I want yours on it in your own words.

What matters most is having the chance for my husband and me to buy the house at a family discount. It would help us build financial independence. We haven’t settled on a price or discount, and C’s agreement is needed; she hasn’t agreed yet.

Hello B. I am sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three sisters agree on a plan for the house. I would like to hear from you directly. What matters most to you about the house and the estate? Is timing or money a concern for you? I am keeping a shared list of everyone's concerns, and I want yours on it in your own words.
What matters most to me is having some money to get my dance studio started. Money is a concern; I’m not sure about timing yet, and I know the value and shares haven’t been decided.

Thank you, A. Here is the draft list of concerns (NCEs). Please tell me if I have worded yours wrongly or missed anything.

NCE 1 (A): A chance for you and your husband to buy the house, at a price that helps you build financial independence.
NCE 2 (C): A fair share based on a proper, independent valuation, with no subsidy of a discount.
NCE 3 (B): Some money to start a dance studio.
NCE 4 (mine): Before any price is agreed, someone should get a copy of the will and confirm who the executor is. I may be wrong that this must come first, so please say if you disagree.

One idea to test: get an independent valuation. You could then buy at that value, and any "discount" would come only from your own share, not from C's or B's. B could take her share in cash from the sale. Does that work for you, and if not, what would?

NCE 1 misses that I’m hoping for a family discount; financial independence is why it matters to me. I don’t know whether B wants the money for a dance studio. An independent valuation could help, but I can’t say the “discount from my share” arrangement works without knowing the shares and how it would be handled. C’s agreement is still needed, and she hasn’t agreed.

Thank you, C. Here is the draft list of concerns (NCEs). Please tell me if I have worded yours wrongly or missed anything.

NCE 1 (A): A chance for A and her husband to buy the house, at a price that helps them build financial independence.
NCE 2 (C): A fair share based on a proper, independent valuation, with no subsidy of a discount.
NCE 3 (B): Some money to start a dance studio.
NCE 4 (mine): Before any price is agreed, someone should get a copy of the will and confirm who the executor is. Please say if you disagree.

One idea to test: get an independent valuation. A could buy at that value, and any "discount" would come only from A's own share, not from yours or B's. B could take her share in cash. Would that meet your concern? Also, would you be willing to ask the family lawyer or the probate court for the will?

NCE 2 is right. An independent valuation and a discount only from A’s own share could work, provided my share isn’t reduced. I’m willing to ask the family lawyer for the will and confirm the executor.

Thank you, B. Here is the draft list of concerns (NCEs). Please tell me if I have worded yours wrongly or missed anything.

NCE 1 (A): A chance for A and her husband to buy the house, at a price that helps them build financial independence.
NCE 2 (C): A fair share based on a proper, independent valuation, with no subsidy of a discount.
NCE 3 (B): Some money to start your dance studio.
NCE 4 (mine): Before any price is agreed, someone should get a copy of the will and confirm who the executor is. Please say if you disagree.

One idea to test: get an independent valuation. A could buy at that value, and any discount would come only from A's own share. You would take your share in cash. Would that work for you? Is there a date by which you need the money?

You’ve captured my concern. I don’t have a date I need the money by. Taking my share in cash might work, but I can’t say until the valuation and everyone’s shares are clear; I don’t know enough to confirm the proposal yet. I don’t disagree with checking the will and executor first.

Thank you, A. I have fixed NCE 1. It now reads: "A and her husband want the chance to buy the house at a family discount, because it would help them build financial independence." B has confirmed that she wants money for a dance studio. I have also added NCE 5 (A): "No one commits to a deal until the shares are known and it is clear how a discount would work."

Next steps: C will ask the family lawyer for the will and confirm the executor. B agrees that should come first. After that, the group can arrange an independent valuation. With the shares known, you can judge whether a discount from your own share is enough, or suggest another option. A mortgage or a payment plan could be ideas to explore. Please tell me if any of this is wrong.

That seems like a sensible process, as long as these are steps to explore, not an agreed deal. I still can’t say whether a discount from my share would be enough, and C’s agreement is needed before we proceed with a purchase.

Thank you, C. Please go ahead and ask the family lawyer for the will and confirm the executor. B agrees this should come first. A has asked to fix NCE 1 so it names the family discount, and I have done that. A also added NCE 5: no one commits until the shares are known and it is clear how a discount would work. B said the same. A has not yet agreed that any discount must come only from her share. She wants to see the shares first. Once you have the will, please share what it says about the house, and we can plan the valuation.
I’ll ask the family lawyer for the will and executor details, then share what it says. NCE 5 makes sense; I won’t agree to a discount that reduces my share.

Thank you, B. Your concern stays as NCE 3, and I have noted that you have no deadline. I added NCE 5: no one commits until the shares are known and it is clear how any discount would work. That matches what you and A both said. C will ask the family lawyer for the will and confirm the executor. Then the group can arrange an independent valuation. Once those are clear, you can decide whether cash fits your studio plans.
That sounds sensible. I’d like to see the valuation and share figures before deciding, and I hope my share will be enough to get the studio started.

Agreed, A. These are steps to explore, not a deal. All three of you now support the same process. First, C gets the will and the executor's details from the family lawyer. Second, the group arranges an independent valuation. Third, everyone looks at the shares and options before anyone commits. No purchase goes ahead without everyone's agreement, including C's.
That captures my understanding: we’ll explore those steps, and no purchase is agreed unless everyone, including C, agrees.
